frame:
SYSTEMIC FRAME — the system prices talents in five currencies, and only one of them is hard-capped per round; the design standard never budgets that one.

A talent costs: an action-type slot (Passive / Special / Free / Action / Reaction), Investiture (leyline+deity), focus (heroic), Opportunity, and occasionally HP. Investiture, focus and Opportunity are POOLS — you bank them, and a tree that overspends them merely runs dry slowly. The action-type slot is not a pool. A character gets 3 Actions per Slow turn and exactly ONE Reaction per round, forever, at every level.

The two design guides regulate the action-type mix as a PER-TREE PERCENTAGE (leyline target: ~35% Passive / 25-30% Special / ~15% Action / ~8% 2-Action / 5-8% Free / 5-8% Reaction / 0% 3-Action). Nothing anywhere converts that percentage into a TURN BUDGET, and no gate checks it. That single omission is the structural cause of most of the ledger, because over-allocation is not symmetric across the row: an extra Passive still delivers its effect; an extra Reaction past the second delivers literally nothing, because the slot is capped at one per round.

Measured against the guide's own table, in TALENTS not percentages (I recomputed this from all-talents.json this session):
  White  Passive +1.3  Special -0.9  Action -2.8  2Act -1.0  Free -1.6  REACTION +5.4
  Blue   Passive +0.3  Special -1.9  Action -0.8  2Act  0.0  Free -0.6  REACTION +3.4
  Black  PASSIVE +6.3  SPECIAL -5.9  Action -0.8  2Act +1.0  Free -0.6  Reaction +0.4
  Red    Passive +2.3  Special +1.1  Action -0.8  2Act -1.0  Free -0.6  Reaction -0.6
  Green  Passive +0.3  Special +0.1  Action -0.8  2Act +1.0  Free -1.6  Reaction +1.4
Three trees are out of spec on the designer's own numbers, and the DIRECTION of each miss predicts the reported symptom exactly. White is five Reactions long and three Actions short — which is ledger item 1, "the two PCs have nothing to spend an Action on," restated as a spec violation rather than a taste judgment. Blue is the same defect one third the size. Black is six Passives long and six Specials short — ledger item 10. Nobody noticed because there is no gate: `scripts/validate.js` checks graph walkability and name resolution, and nothing checks the action mix.

The purest illustration is White's level-2 band. Interposing Shield, Retributive Guard and Shared Burden are three separate talents, all Reactions, all costing Investiture, and all triggered by the SAME event ("an ally [within 10 ft / adjacent] takes damage"). A White player at level 6 owns all three and may use one. Three of twenty-five slots deliver one slot of throughput. Meanwhile the same player has one Action talent (Guiding Signal, L1) and gets their second at level 4.

Four further system-level facts compound it, each of which also collapses several ledger items:

(1) BINARY ADVANTAGE IS THE ONLY GENERIC "MAKE A ROLL BETTER" PRIMITIVE, AND IT SATURATES AT ONE. 36-45 talents produce it; the engine boolean-ORs them (`edhaNextModFoldMode`). Every tree reaches for it because it is the cheap generic buff, so every tree builds redundancy into itself and into every other tree. The engine ALREADY ships a summing alternative — `edha-next-test-mod` with a `formula` field, made additive by item 49 — used by one adversary ability and by zero talents. The system has a second scalar channel and is not using it. Leader's command die is the only talent-side proof that the channel is fun, and it is hand-rolled.

(2) LEVEL 6 IS A TRIPLE STEP AND LEVELS 1-5 ARE FLAT. Tier goes 1→2 (dice count doubles), rank cap goes 2→3 (die goes d6→d8), and 5-8 rank-3-gated talents per tree unlock — all on the same level. Leyline/deity output ×2.57 in one step; heroic damage formulas move by ×1.00 because their tier terms are `max(@tier - 2, 0)`, dead until level 11. The system has exactly one scaling knob and it fires once in the campaign's ten levels.

(3) THE DEITY TOLL IS PRICED IN THE SAME CURRENCY THAT SIZES THE DAMAGE DIE, AND ONLY ONE COLOUR CASHES. Entry gates demand `[C1] 2+; [C2] 2+` = four skill ranks (two levels of skill income) and every deity formula is `(@tier)d(2 * @skills.<ONE colour>.rank + 2)`. Rank 3 in both = six ranks for a die that reads one of them. No card names which colour, so the player buying the third rank is choosing blind.

(4) CONTINGENT OUTPUT IS PRICED AT THE SAME RATE AS UNCONDITIONAL OUTPUT. There is no discount rule. White's Interposing Shield costs 1 Investiture and waits for an ally to be hit; Red's Searing Bolt costs 1 Investiture and just happens. 22 of White's 25 talents need a second body present; 0 of Chaos's, Death's and Destruction's do. This is why trees whose output routes through other characters feel weak independently of their actual numbers, and it is why the fifteen-axis rubric scored Sovereignty (a pure through-ally amplifier) at damage_direct 0 while scoring Knowledge (the identical machine that also holds a sword) at 5.

WHAT THIS FRAME PREDICTS, AND WHY IT MATTERS FOR THE LIVE DECISION: "add damage to Blue and White" is a symptom-shaped fix. Of the 116 repeatable, self-initiated, Action-costing talents in the corpus, 54 deal damage — damage is simply the category the system has actually implemented as an unconditional, repeatable, on-your-own-turn play. Adding damage to White would give a White player something to do with an Action; so would adding anything else that is unconditional, repeatable and Action-costing. The damage is incidental to the cure.

proposals.title: Make the action-type target table a BUDGET with a floor and a cap, gate it in CI, and let the gate drive a re-typing pass on White, Blue and Black
proposals.change: Three parts. (a) Add two hard rules to both design guides, replacing the soft percentage targets for the two capped slots: **REACTION CAP — no tree may field more than 3 Reaction talents, and no two Reactions in a tree may share a trigger class**; **ACTION FLOOR — every tree must field at least 3 repeatable (not once-per-scene), self-initiated, Action-costing talents whose earliest level is 3 or below.** Repeatable + self-initiated is defined mechanically: activationType is an Action or 2-Action, the text contains no 'once per scene', and the effect resolves without requiring another creature to act first. (b) Write `scripts/validate-action-budget.js`, add it to `scripts/gates.js` and `validate.yml`: it reads all-talents.json, prints the per-tree deviation table I computed in the frame, and FAILS on a Reaction count above 3, on two Reactions sharing a trigger regex, or on an Action floor below 3-by-L3. (c) Run the pass the gate demands. White: retype 4 of 7 Reactions — collapse the three same-trigger damage Reactions (Interposing Shield, Retributive Guard, Shared Burden) into one Reaction plus two always-on Passives or Specials, and move Voice of Authority and Pillar of Order onto the same consolidation; then convert two of the surplus Specials into 1-Action plays so the floor is met by L3. Blue: retype 2 of 5 Reactions (Redirect Momentum and False Premise both fire on another creature's turn and both duplicate Blue's disadvantage channel). Black: convert 6 of 15 Passives to Specials per Revision Principle 4.
proposals.resolves: Ledger 1 (directly and completely — this IS the two PCs' dead turn), 10 (Black's 60% Passive / 4% Special), 15 (Interposing Shield's `half [Die]` stops mattering once the three same-trigger Reactions are consolidated), and structurally 8 (the same gate, pointed at the deity atlas, catches the 0-Specials-in-90 miss). It also permanently prevents the class of defect rather than fixing three instances of it.
proposals.cost: White loses roughly four talent slots' worth of NOMINAL breadth and gains three usable Actions — a White player at level 6 who currently owns three ally-damage Reactions and uses one will instead own one Reaction plus two always-on mitigations, which is a straight power INCREASE, so retest White's survivability contribution before assuming it is neutral. Blue is near-neutral. Black gets action-efficiency it did not have, which is a real buff to the tree the review already flags as holding the game's best control talent and its only 2x-tier damage formula (ledger 17) — sequence this after, or alongside, a Withering Ray ruling. Retest: every retyped talent's Foundry wiring (a Reaction handler becoming a Passive or Special is a different activation path), the White Reaction-slot behaviour at the bench, and every ledger figure that summed White mitigation over rounds. Iron rule 7 exposure is nil — no `connections` edges move.
proposals.confidence: HIGH on the diagnosis, HIGH on the gate, MEDIUM on the specific retyping choices. The deviation table is computed from the shipped data against a target the designer wrote, so the miss is not a matter of taste. What would change my mind: if Ben says the Reaction target of 5-8% was itself the mistake and White is deliberately a bodyguard whose seven Reactions are meant as COVERAGE across five trigger classes rather than seven uses. That defence is on the table and it is partly right — but it cannot survive the three same-trigger talents, which are coverage of nothing.
proposals.surface: DATA (talent action types + authored activation, pack rebuild + Sync) plus ONE new gate script; spot ENGINE work only where a Reaction handler must become a Passive/Special activation path

proposals.title: Wire the summing numeric roll-modifier channel that already exists in the engine, and make it — not binary advantage — the home for stacking buffs and debuffs
proposals.change: Ruling first: **advantage/disadvantage stays the binary 'you got a break' flag and is granted at most once per tree per trigger; magnitude that is meant to STACK moves to a numeric `[Die]`-denominated channel.** Implementation: `edha-next-test-mod` already carries a `formula` field whose matching entries SUM by term concatenation (item 49); it is used by one adversary ability (`Probability Net`) and by zero talents. (a) Add a CAP to that primitive in the engine — the summed formula on any one roll may not exceed `[Tier][Die]` in either direction — and pin a regression test in `tests/`. (b) Convert the colliding advantage/disadvantage producers onto it. The priority set is Blue's five disadvantage talents (Pattern Recognition, False Premise, Intercept, Voice-of-Authority-adjacent, and its Key rider), which today collapse into one another; each becomes `-1d6` and they sum. (c) Register the channel in `ENGINE_INDEX.md` so future authoring reaches for it instead of reflexively writing 'gain an advantage'.
proposals.resolves: Ledger 14 outright (Fatal Thrust's 'two advantages' and Defensive Position's 'two disadvantages' become expressible rather than false card text), the 'advantage over-produced, 45 talents / 13 trees' finding in the resource census, and the redundancy half of ledger 13. Most importantly it hands leyline/Blue a REPEATABLE, SELF-INITIATED, ESCALATING, LEGIBLE play that is not damage — which is the actual cure for ledger 1's Blue half and the reason I do not recommend giving Blue damage.
proposals.cost: This is the ecosystem's largest identified balance risk and the defence advocate is right to name it: converting binary grants into summing ones trades a 'does nothing' problem for a potentially unbounded 'does too much' one. The `[Tier][Die]` cap is the mitigation and it must ship in the same change, not after. Blue becomes the game's clear best debuffer, which is intended but changes every Blue-vs-Scholar and Blue-vs-Black comparison in the review. The primitive is UNPROVEN on talents — one adversary ability is the entire production evidence — so the first conversion needs a bench run before the other four land. Retest: the fold logic in `15-blue-calculation.js` alongside the summing path (the two must not double-count), and every talent that reads 'has advantage' as a trigger.
proposals.confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH that the channel is the right answer; MEDIUM that Blue is the right first consumer. What would change my mind: a bench measurement showing the summed formula does not actually apply through the cosmere-rpg roll pipeline for player talents the way it does for the adversary ability — that is a two-minute check and it must be run before any authoring.
proposals.surface: ENGINE (cap + regression test + verifying the talent-side path) then DATA (authored events on ~10-15 talents, pack rebuild + Sync)

proposals.title: Change the signature-resource cap denominator from `tier` to `tier + 1`, in one sweep across all six deity trees that use it
proposals.change: Six deity trees cap their signature token at 'up to your tier': Chaos (Omens), Order (Edicts AND Covenants), Civilization (Foundations), Destruction (Charges), Fate (Ordained Ground AND Snares), Death (Risen Servants). Tier is 1 for the whole of levels 1-5, so the cap is ONE for half the campaign. Replace every one of these with `1 + your tier` (2 at Tier 1, 3 at Tier 2). Do the same to Civilization's Forge Construct, which is the one outlier — it reads 'You may sustain one active Construct', a flat 1 that never scales at all, uniquely among the ten sustain clauses. Card text + the authored formulas where the cap is machine-read.
proposals.resolves: Ledger 12 entirely. Downstream, it makes castable or non-dominated: Civilization's Trade Routes (currently UNCASTABLE below level 6 — it requires two active Foundations), Chaos's Spreading Omen (currently dominated by its own entry), Chaos's Cascade Collapse and Unravel Everything (currently single-target through L5 despite being the tree's AoE), Destruction's Cascading Failure ('when two or more Charges detonate' — currently impossible at Tier 1) and The Unmooring, Order's Lawkeeper's Eye and Final Decree. It also partially resolves ledger 2 (target count): two of the corpus's few multi-enemy talents are Chaos's Omen detonations, which are single-target at Tier 1 purely because of this cap.
proposals.cost: Six deity trees get materially stronger at levels 1-5, which is exactly the level band this campaign is in. That is the point — but it means deity-vs-leyline parity at Tier 1 shifts, and the deity atlas is already the most Action-dense (72% of slots) in the game. If the designer's intent was that the cap IS the level-6 step change (the defence advocate's reading), this proposal deliberately removes it, and the compensating lever is the die-size step, which still doubles at 6. Retest: every downstream talent listed above, and the sustain arithmetic in Order (two independent tier-capped pools becomes two 2-caps at Tier 1).
proposals.confidence: HIGH that the current state is broken (a talent that cannot be cast at its own earliest level is not a pacing decision), MEDIUM on `tier + 1` as the right denominator versus a flat 2/3 ladder or `rank - 1`. What would change my mind: if Ben confirms the level-6 discontinuity is deliberately three-fold and he wants deity trees to feel thin until 6.
proposals.surface: DATA (domain.json card text + data/authored/deity-*.json formulas, pack rebuild + Sync)

proposals.title: Stop charging for a deity colour the tree cannot cash: make the deity damage die read the higher of the two gate colours, and print the scaling colour on every card
proposals.change: Two parts, separable. (a) ENGINE/formula: change every deity damage and heal formula from `(@tier)d(2 * @skills.<fixed colour>.rank + 2)` to read the MAXIMUM of the tree's two gate colours. Either emit `max(@skills.a.rank, @skills.b.rank)` inline in the 30-odd deity formulas, or add one derived accessor and point all of them at it. (b) DATA, independently valuable: print the scaling colour on the card. Every deity card today says '[Tier][Die]' with no colour, so a player deciding between a third rank of Black and a third of White is choosing blind — this is the real finding under the disputed 'toll booth' headline, and it is a one-word-per-card fix.
proposals.resolves: The toll-booth family in ledger 4 and the completeness critic's correction of it — the honest count after reading BOTH the `@skills.<c>.rank` formulas and the `color`/`rangeColor` targeting fields is ONE pure toll booth (Fate/White, zero references of any kind) plus three near-dead gates (Sovereignty/White 1 ref, Destruction/Blue 1, Life/Blue 1). Part (a) dissolves all four at once instead of hand-patching each tree. Part (b) dissolves the card-blindness that made the toll problem invisible, and it costs nothing and needs no ruling.
proposals.cost: Part (a) is a straight power increase to every deity tree — a character who bought rank 3 in the 'wrong' colour now gets 2d8 where they got 1d6 — and it weakens the design intent that each deity tree tests its own colours (deity guide: 'Black tests for diminish; White tests for elevate'). It also removes the only current mechanical reason to care WHICH colour you deepen, which is arguably the interesting decision. A cheaper alternative that keeps the tension: make the ENTRY gate asymmetric — `[colour that sizes the die] 2+; [other colour] 1+` — cutting the toll from four skill ranks to three and from six to four at rank 3. Retest: every deity damage formula, and the Sovereignty temp-HP formula which uniquely reads White. Part (b) has no cost at all.
proposals.confidence: HIGH on part (b), which I would ship on its own tomorrow. MEDIUM on part (a) — I think the asymmetric-gate variant is probably better design than the max-of-two variant, because it keeps the colour choice meaningful while halving the price. What would change my mind on (a): if Ben says the two-colour cost IS the deity trees' balancing price and they are meant to be expensive.
proposals.surface: (a) DATA-heavy formula edit across ten data/authored/deity-*.json files, possibly one ENGINE accessor; (b) pure DATA (card text, pack rebuild + Sync)

proposals.title: Give White, Blue and Green the bonus Investiture regeneration that Black, Red and five deity trees already have — or raise Draw Mana to `tier + 1`
proposals.change: The corpus has exactly nine bonus-Investiture producers and their distribution is the inverse of need: Black 2 regen / 9 costers (plus HP as an alternate currency on Withering Ray), Red 2 / 9, and then White 0 / 15, Blue 0 / 16 (sixteen — Counterspell's cost field reads '1 Investiure', which is why every regex census misses it), Green 0 / 13. Five of ten deity trees carry a FREE depth-1 Passive regen keyed to their own mark taking damage (Chaos Void Sense, Death Reaper's Harvest, Life Prognosis, Knowledge Accumulate, Sovereignty Expose) — that is a template, and it is unused by the three leyline trees that most need it. Option A (per-tree, DATA): give White, Blue and Green each one free depth-1 Passive regen on the same template, keyed to something the tree already does (White: an ally you healed via the Key being damaged; Blue: a creature failing a test you imposed disadvantage on; Green: a creature entering your difficult terrain). Option B (system-wide, ENGINE): change `edhaDrawMana` in `module-src/scripts/engine/52-green-instinct.js` to return `tier + 1`, so refuelling costs 1 Action for 2 Investiture at Tier 1 instead of 1-for-1.
proposals.resolves: The 50%-uptime throttle the primer derives and names ('bonus-regen talents are the lever that breaks this; count them' — I counted, and the three trees with zero are the three the review is worried about). It resolves the second half of ledger 1's Blue case: Blue's problem is not only that it has few Action plays, it is that its 16 costers against zero regen make the ones it has intermittent. It also removes the 'contingent trees are also the poorest' compounding effect described in the frame.
proposals.cost: Option B buffs every leyline and deity character in the game by roughly a third of an Action per round and would need every 'rounds of play' figure in this review recomputed; it also makes Black's HP-for-Investiture identity less distinctive, and Black is the tree that already has the game's only unlimited damage line. Option A is surgical but adds three talents' worth of power to three trees and needs three slots freed to hold them. Retest under B: every Investiture arithmetic in the review, plus the deity trees, which are the heaviest spenders (Power 15 Investiture to install, zero returned).
proposals.confidence: HIGH that the asymmetry is real and unintended (nothing in either guide says White and Blue should be the poorest); MEDIUM-LOW on Option B, which I would not do without a bench pass, because it touches all fifteen magical trees at once. Option A is the safer half. What would change my mind: if the three zero-regen trees turn out to spend their Investiture almost entirely on Reactions and Specials — which for White is largely TRUE (15 costers, only 2 Action talents), meaning White's Investiture is not competing with its Actions and the throttle bites Blue and Green harder than White.
proposals.surface: Option A = DATA (three new authored talents, pack rebuild + Sync); Option B = ENGINE (one function, `edhaDrawMana`)

proposals.title: Write a contingency-pricing rule into both guides: an effect that waits on another creature costs one step less than the same effect on your own turn
proposals.change: Add to both design standards, beside the existing cost scale ('1 = routine, 2 = significant, 3 = a big play'): **a talent whose payoff requires another character to act, be hit, fail, or be present costs one step less than the same magnitude delivered unconditionally; a Reaction that also costs an action-type slot capped at one per round costs one step less again, to a floor of free.** Then sweep the ~60 contingent talents and re-price. The clearest instances: White's Interposing Shield (1 Investiture, waits for an ally to be hit, mitigates `half [Die]`) against Devoted Conduit and Shield Wall (free, permanent, mitigate `half [Tier][Die]`) — the costed contingent one is worth less than half the free unconditional one at Tier 2; Fate's whole ally-triggered half; Order's Covenant chain; Sovereignty's five ally-dependent talents.
proposals.resolves: Ledger 15 (Interposing Shield) as an instance of a rule rather than a typo, and the systemic reason the rubric and the reviewers both scored contingent trees low — it gives the design a lever that makes a bodyguard tree feel fairly paid instead of taxed twice. It also removes the pressure to 'fix' White and Sovereignty by making them do something different, when what they actually do is under-compensated.
proposals.cost: A broad re-pricing pass across roughly a sixth of the corpus, each of which needs its authored cost field and card text changed together, and it makes White, Fate, Order and Sovereignty cheaper to operate — i.e. stronger — without changing what they do. The risk is double-dipping with proposal 1, which already increases White's throughput by consolidating same-trigger Reactions; do not run both on White without re-measuring in between. Retest: every 'rounds of play' figure for the affected trees.
proposals.confidence: MEDIUM. The asymmetry is real and I can name instances, but I cannot show that a one-step discount is the right exchange rate, and nothing inside the 365-talent fence can — that needs table play. What would change my mind: a bench or playtest showing contingent talents actually fire often enough that they are fairly priced today.
proposals.surface: DATA (cost fields + card text across ~60 talents, pack rebuild + Sync) plus a guide edit

proposals.title: Decide a target-count budget at the SYSTEM level and give the leyline Attunement Keys the multi-target valve, rather than adding AoE talents to fourteen trees
proposals.change: Fourteen of twenty-one trees can never damage two enemies with one play at any level, and five of six heroic paths have literally zero (the sixth has one: Warrior's Meteoric Leap, depth 3, Athletics 3+, level 6, unarmed). Before authoring anything, get a ruling on the budget: what fraction of trees should be able to threaten a group, and at what level. Then, if the answer is 'more than two', the systemic lever is already sitting in the primer: **[Size]** (2.5/5/10/15/20 ft by rank) is a defined scaling term used by very few talents, and the Attunement Keys are free, always-on, and fire on an action every leyline character already takes. Green's Key already creates a [Size] zone on Draw Mana — that is the template. A parallel clause on one or two other Keys, or a general authoring rule ('any single-target talent may instead be authored to [Size] of a point for +1 Investiture'), gives the whole leyline atlas a multi-target valve without writing fourteen new talents. Separately and regardless: leyline/Black's Spoils of Isolation is built backwards — it damages 'each Weakened character', and Black's only two Weakened sources both require the target to have NO ally within 5 feet, so Black's area attack scales with how spread out the enemies are and does nothing to a clump. Fix that one by changing what it keys on.
proposals.resolves: Ledger 2, which no analysis raised and which is an encounter-design constraint rather than a balance question — it says the GM cannot put four enemies on the table without the fight becoming a queue, for the specific party this review was commissioned about.
proposals.cost: Any real answer here adds power broadly. The Key route is the cheapest but touches the one talent every character of a colour holds, so it is the highest-blast-radius data edit in this list. The [Size] authoring rule risks AoE proliferation with no per-tree cap. The Spoils of Isolation fix is small and safe.
proposals.confidence: LOW-MEDIUM on the remedy, HIGH on the census. This is the one place where the scope fence genuinely binds: whether fourteen zero-AoE trees is a defect depends on whether groups of minions are the encounter norm, and that lives in adversary statblocks, which are explicitly out of scope. What would settle it: the adversary pack's group-size distribution, or two sessions of play.
proposals.surface: DATA if the Key/[Size] route is taken (pack rebuild + Sync); the ruling itself is the deliverable of this pass

proposals.title: Unify the three temporary-HP behaviours in the engine before anyone does temp-HP arithmetic again
proposals.change: Three positions are live simultaneously. `module-src/scripts/engine/28-temporary-hp.js` contradicts ITSELF seven lines apart — line 6 says 'the pool does not stack, a larger grant replaces a smaller one', line 13 says 'a new grant OVERWRITES the old, even if smaller' — and the code implements the second (`edhaWriteTempHp` sets unconditionally). `module-src/scripts/engine/51-green-restoration.js:93` `edhaGrantTempHpCross` implements keep-the-higher (`wins = inc > (held?.value ?? 0)`, 'A TIE is not a win'). And `data/authored/deity-sovereignty.json` asserts keep-the-higher in the description of the very talent whose swing arithmetic the deity-parity analysis computed using overwrite-even-if-smaller. Pick one, make both writers call it, fix the header comment, pin a regression test.
proposals.resolves: Ledger 7, and it retroactively validates or invalidates every temp-HP figure in the review (Order's Bear Witness, Sovereignty's swing, Life's overflow). 14 talents across 9 trees produce temp HP.
proposals.cost: Almost none — this is engineering hygiene. The only design consequence is which rule is canon; keep-the-higher is the one the data already assumes and the one that does not punish a player for being helped twice.
proposals.confidence: HIGH. The contradiction is verbatim in the source. What would change my mind: nothing about the defect; only the choice of canon rule is a judgment, and it is a small one.
proposals.surface: ENGINE (two writers + header comment + a pinned regression case in tests/)

proposals.title: Close the determinable data defects as one themed sweep, and add the ungated iron-rule-7 check that would have caught two of them
proposals.change: Nine items, all determinable, none needing a ruling. (1) deity/Death Raise Dead: card says 'Necrotic Cascade or Speak with the Fallen', `connections` is ['Necrotic Cascade','Risen Servant'] — Foundry demands a talent the card never names. (2) deity/Death Necrotic Cascade: card says 'Consuming Decay', `connections` silently ANDs Death Ward. (3) Write the gate iron rule 7 says does not exist — a checker that compares each talent's prose prerequisite names against its `connections` array and fails on divergence; `validateConnections` only checks that a name resolves, and the DAG/reachability checks only catch cycles. (4) `data/leyline.json:840` Counterspell cost 'Investiure' → 'Investiture' (permanently corrupts every Blue census). (5) leyline/White Interposing Shield `half [Die]` → `half [Tier][Die]` to match its two siblings. (6) deity/Chaos Unravel Everything: add 'once per scene' — it is the only one of ten deity capstones without it. (7) deity/Power Kneel and Absolute Authority name Frightened, which no talent in the corpus produces; either cut the word or give something a Frightened application. (8) leyline/White Shared Burden's `rankGate` is 'Strength 3+; White 2+' and the tooling has applied the SKILL rank cap to an attribute — Strength is an attribute (the primer's own `Health = 10 + STR`), attribute points arrive at 3/6/9, so its earliest level needs re-deriving. (9) leyline/White Mending Aura: the authored text costs Opportunity AND 1 Investiture, the source prose costs Opportunity only; the authored text wins in Foundry, so the source prose owes a fix.
proposals.resolves: Ledger 5, 9, 15, 16, 18, 20, and part of 4. Item (3) is the systemic half — it closes the third, ungated case that CLAUDE.md's iron rule 7 explicitly warns about, so the next divergence fails a gate instead of failing a player.
proposals.cost: Trivial, and item (3) is the only one with any risk: the new gate will probably flag the third non-fatal case the rule already names (prose and `connections` naming different parents, which silently ANDs them — Green's Scent the Weak and Coordinated Hunt), so budget a triage pass before turning it from warn to fail.
proposals.confidence: HIGH on all nine. Every one was read from the shipped data.
proposals.surface: DATA (domain.json, leyline.json, authored overlays — pack rebuild + Sync) plus one new gate script

proposals.title: Decouple the level-6 triple step by moving the rank-3 GATES off it, leaving the die/tier step where it is
proposals.change: At level 6, three things fire at once: tier 1→2 (dice count doubles), rank cap 2→3 (die d6→d8), and 5-8 rank-3-gated talents per tree unlock. The product is ×2.57 on every leyline and deity formula, plus a bolus of new options, in one level. Do not touch [Tier][Die] — it is the system's only scaling knob and 43 formulas read it. Instead thin the third component: replace 'Colour 3+' prerequisites on deep leyline nodes with a mix of 'Colour 2+' plus a longer talent chain, so unlock timing spreads across levels 4-8 instead of piling on 6. This also directly fixes several dated-L6 talents whose gate is pacing rather than power (leyline/Blue has EIGHT rank-3 gates, the most in the atlas, and its three teeth — Counterspell, Ghostly Walls, Anticipate — are all L6, which is the real reason Blue's kit does not assemble until half the campaign is over).
proposals.resolves: Ledger 3's felt half, and the second half of ledger 1's Blue case (Blue has five Action talents but three of them are scene-setup and its repeatable ones arrive at L4 and L6). Note what it does NOT resolve: the heroic-vs-leyline SCALING asymmetry, which is a formula fact and which the defence advocate correctly argues cannot be settled inside the 365-talent fence because heroic damage rides on weapon dice that are out of scope.
proposals.cost: Moves ~30 talents' earliest levels and therefore invalidates every pacing figure in the review. It also weakens the guide's Revision Principle 5 ('3rd-node-and-beyond talents should gate on skill investment'). Iron rule 7 exposure is real: any prerequisite edit that touches `connections` must be re-validated against the DAG and reachability gates. Retest: the whole earliest-level derivation, plus a rerun of the deviation table in the frame.
proposals.confidence: MEDIUM. That level 6 is a triple step is a fact; that spreading the gates is better than the discontinuity is a design judgment I cannot settle from the data, and there is a real argument that a big level-6 moment is GOOD. What would change my mind: Ben saying the level-6 spike is the intended payoff for five flat levels.
proposals.surface: DATA (prerequisites in leyline.json/domain.json + `connections`, pack rebuild + Sync)

singleFirstChange:
Retype leyline/White's action mix against the guide's own target table — specifically, collapse the three same-trigger Reactions (Interposing Shield, Retributive Guard, Shared Burden, all firing on "an ally takes damage") into ONE Reaction plus two always-on Passives/Specials, and convert two of White's six Specials into 1-Action plays reachable by level 3. That is proposal 1(c), White only.

Why this one and not the gate, the ruling, or anything about damage: it is the only change on the list that acts directly on the thing the designer actually noticed, on the specific character who noticed it, at the specific levels being played, without needing a single ruling and without inventing anything. White is -2.8 Action talents and +5.4 Reactions against a target Ben wrote himself, and the three same-trigger Reactions are the defect in its purest form — three of twenty-five slots delivering one slot of throughput, because the Reaction slot is capped at one per round. Nothing about it depends on any disputed measurement in this review: not the earliest-level tooling, not Momentum's Edge, not the temp-HP writers, not the cosine matrix, not the toll-booth count. It adds zero damage, changes no identity, moves no `connections` edge, and it is testable at the bench the same evening.

The gate (proposal 1a/1b) is the more valuable change in the long run and should follow within the same work item — but a gate that fails three trees on day one is a backlog, whereas a White player with three usable Actions is a fixed table.
argumentOnBlueWhiteDamage:
POSITION: NO. Do not give leyline/Blue or leyline/White damage. Give them Action-costing plays. The two are being confused because of an accident of what the system has actually implemented, not because damage is what is missing.

THE ARGUMENT, in the order it has to be made.

1. The complaint is not "I do no damage." I recomputed the action-cost census over all 365 talents: leyline/White fields TWO talents in twenty-five that a player can spend an Action on — Guiding Signal (1 Action, level 1) and Ordered Advance (2 Actions, level 4, and conditional on you moving). leyline/Blue fields five, of which three are scene-setup (Phantom Double, Telepathic Network, Phantom Barricade) and the two repeatable ones arrive at levels 4 and 6. Every deity tree fields five to eight in NINE slots. heroic/Warrior fields thirteen. A White PC's turn at level 3 is: Draw Mana, then two Actions their sheet gives them nothing to do with. That is what "my character does nothing" means at the table, and it would be exactly as true if you handed them a damage talent they could only use as a Reaction.

2. Damage looks like the answer because damage is the only thing the system has implemented as an unconditional, repeatable, self-initiated Action play. Of the 116 repeatable Action-costing talents in the corpus, 54 deal damage. Control, buff, protection and healing exist in volume, but they are overwhelmingly authored as Reactions, Passives or Specials — i.e. as things that wait for someone else. So "add damage to White" is really "add an unconditional repeatable Action play to White," wearing a costume. Recognising that frees you to pick the version that does not break White's identity.

3. Both trees' binding intent sources are explicitly damage-free and both deliver something genuinely theirs. INTENT-leyline-Blue.md: "They rarely meet force with force." INTENT-leyline-White.md: "A White mage rarely wins alone." Blue is the only tree in all 365 talents that CREATES illusions, and Counterspell is the only talent that makes another character's talent fail as it is being activated. White's Attunement Key is the only Draw Mana rider that pays the whole party, and it is the only tree whose refuel Action is itself an effect — a White player's Draw Mana turn heals every ally in range AND, with Beacon of Stability, strips a condition. These are not empty trees. They are trees whose output has been routed almost entirely into slots that are capped or contingent.

4. What to do instead, concretely, and it is already in the proposal list. For WHITE: proposal 1(c) — three of its seven Reactions fire on the same event and two of them can become always-on Passives or Specials at no identity cost, freeing slots; then convert two Specials into 1-Action plays. White does not need a new mechanic; it needs its existing mitigation to stop competing with itself for one slot per round. For BLUE: proposal 2 — move Blue's five binary-disadvantage talents onto the summing `edha-next-test-mod` numeric channel that already exists in the engine and is used by zero talents. Today Blue's five disadvantage talents largely do one talent's work, because advantage and disadvantage are a single tri-state the engine boolean-ORs. On a summing `-1d6` channel they become a repeatable, self-initiated, ESCALATING, legible play — a number that goes up as you invest, which is precisely the psychological thing damage provides and the thing binary disadvantage cannot provide no matter how many talents you write.

5. The one place I would concede damage, and I do not think it is here. If playtest confirms ledger item 2 — that a party drawn from these twenty-one trees has no answer to a group of enemies — the fix is AREA damage, not single-target damage, and White is a defensible home for it (its Key already reaches the whole party, and Green's Key already proves the [Size]-zone-on-Draw-Mana template works). Even then I would put it on Green or Red first, and I would want the adversary group-size distribution before authoring anything, which is outside this review's fence.

6. What would change my mind. Two things, both cheap to check. (a) If Ben runs a White PC through two sessions AFTER the Reaction consolidation and still reports a dead turn, then the agency diagnosis is wrong and the tree needs new content rather than re-typed content — at which point damage is back on the table as one option among several. (b) If the bench shows the summing numeric channel does not actually apply to player talents the way it applies to the one adversary ability that uses it, then Blue loses its non-damage cure and the honest answer for Blue changes. That is a two-minute check and it should be run before anything else in proposal 2.
argumentOnSovereignty:
deity/Sovereignty is the one tree where I would NOT reach for a systemic fix, because two of its three problems are its own and only one is systemic.

The systemic one is the frame's point (4), contingency pricing: Sovereignty is the purest through-ally amplifier in the game — five of nine talents need a willing ally in Attunement Range — and both the fifteen-axis rubric and every analyst penalised it for delivering damage through someone else's hand. deity/Knowledge runs the identical machine (mark a creature, multiply the party's damage against it) and scores damage_direct 5 because it also holds a sword. Same function, opposite score. Proposal 6 is the right systemic answer to that half, and proposal 4(b) — print the scaling colour on the card — fixes the specific card-blindness that made its White 3+ gate look inert when in fact `data/authored/deity-sovereignty.json` contains one `@skills.white.rank`, sizing Sovereign's Favor's temp HP as `(@tier)d(2 * @skills.white.rank + 2)`. That is a real reward for the gate and no card says so.

The two problems that are Sovereignty's own, and that no system rule dissolves:

(a) DECREE DOES NOT EXIST. Both intent sources promise a declared law projected within a radius — allies inside elevated, enemies inside diminished — and the deity guide names the loop "diminish target → elevate ally → bring them into Decree." All nine talents target "a creature in Attunement Range" or "a willing ally"; searching the tree for radius/aura/zone/area returns nothing, and the word "Decree" appears only inside the talent name "Decree of Ruin." A player meets this promise before they ever roll a die, because the path description is what they read when choosing a god. This is a DOCUMENTATION defect if the guide is wrong and a DESIGN defect if the guide is right, and it needs a ruling to say which — but note that unlike the disputed Blue/plot-die case, the deity guide's Part 4 carries NO "reference, not law" disclaimer, so this drift is real where that one may not be.

(b) THE PAYLOAD IS SUB-PERCEPTUAL AND THE TREE IS BUILT FROM TWO CLAUSES. One die step is +1.0 average per die, and against the four flat-damage riders in the corpus (Momentum of Victory, Cheap Shot, Pack Share, Vital Diagnosis) it is worth exactly zero. Eight of the nine talents are assembled from "damage die size increases by one step (max d12)" or "decreases by one step (min d4)". Worse, the two biggest elevate effects compete for the same headroom — Investiture of Authority (+1 for the scene) and the capstone (+2 for the scene) cannot both pay out on a rank-3 ally rolling d8, because there are only two rungs to the cap. No system rule fixes a signature mechanic whose unit of effect is below the threshold at which a human at a table notices anything happened.

MY POSITION: Sovereignty needs a design pass, not a system pass, and it is the one tree in the review I would say that about. The sequence is: get the Decree ruling (does the promise stand, and does the tree get zones?), then either build Decree as a real [Size] zone — which would also give the tree the multi-target capability fourteen trees lack, and is the single best place in the corpus to prototype proposal 7's [Size] valve — or amend both intent sources to describe the single-target arbiter the tree actually is. Do not do the second unless you also fix the payload, because a tree that is honestly described as "changes one die size by one step" is a tree nobody will pick. And do NOT ship any temp-HP arithmetic about this tree until proposal 8 lands: Sovereign's Favor's own authored description asserts keep-the-higher on a talent the engine's main writer overwrites even if smaller, which is exactly the contradiction that invalidated the previous swing calculations.
